title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees, managers, and auditors.

Scope: Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and approved vendors interacting with Redwood systems or representing Redwood externally.

Owners and governance
- Primary owner: People Ops (owner_team)
- Security owner: InfoSec (security-and-compliance)
- Finance owner: Finance & Legal
- Review cadence: Annual review by People Ops + Security + Finance; ad-hoc reviews after major incidents or regulatory changes.

1) Access and permissions
- Principle: Least privilege by default. Access must be granted only for the minimum time and scope required.
- Role definitions (examples):
  - Employee: standard corporate apps, documentation, limited production read access where required for role.
  - SRE/Platform: CI/CD systems, production metrics, runbook editing, limited write to deployment orchestration.
  - ML Engineer: model artifacts, staging environments, metrics; production write only with approval.
  - Admin: limited to designated admin roster with 2FA and justifications recorded.
- Provisioning process (standard):
  1. Request via internal IAM portal with justification, owner, and requested duration.
  2. Manager approval (auto-deny after 7 days without approval).
  3. Security review for any production write or cross-tenant access.
  4. Provisioning executed by platform-ops; change logged in access-audit stream.
- Temporary access: Time-boxed approvals (max 14 days for non-emergent requests). Requests >14 days require quarterly review.
- Privileged access:
  - All privileged accounts require hardware-backed 2FA or SSO with MFA.
  - Privileged access requests must include rollback plan and an explicit owner.
- Deprovisioning: Offboarding checklist triggers deprovisioning within 24 hours of termination/contract end. Team leads must confirm access removal in the offboarding form.
- Audit & reporting: Quarterly access reviews by team owners; annual third-party access audit for enterprise customers under NDA.

2) Change management (infrastructure, runtime, and config)
- Objective: Reduce risk to production while enabling rapid delivery.
- Change categories:
  - Standard change: Low-risk, pre-authorized (e.g., minor config flips <5% user impact).
  - Normal change: Requires approval from Change Approver Board (CAB) with testing evidence.
  - Emergency change: Applied to remediate critical incidents; must be documented and reviewed within 72 hours post-change.
- Pre-deployment requirements for Normal changes:
  - Design doc or PR explaining impact, rollback plan, and verification steps.
  - Test plan: unit/integration tests + canary/blue-green rollout plan where applicable.
  - Risk classification (low/medium/high) and required approvers.
- CAB membership and cadence: Weekly CAB meeting, ad-hoc for high-severity requests. CAB includes representatives from SRE, Platform, Security, and Product.
- Rollout patterns: Canary (recommended), A/B, or feature-flagged blue/green for runtime changes. Metrics to watch during rollout: error rate, latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, and cost per 1k requests.
- Emergency change workflow:
  1. Notify oncall and create incident ticket.
  2. Implement minimal change to remediate.
  3. Postmortem and retro within 3 business days; document change rationale and follow-up actions.

3) Data management (classification, retention, handling)
- Classification levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Sensitive.
  - Public: marketing materials, public docs.
  - Internal: internal wiki, non-sensitive telemetry.
  - Confidential: customer contracts, pricing, non-PHI customer data.
  - Sensitive: PII, PHI, encryption keys, raw model training datasets containing personal data.
- Storage and handling rules:
  - Confidential and Sensitive data must be encrypted at rest and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
  - Access to Sensitive data requires explicit approval and logging at request-level.
  - Local persistence: No Sensitive or Confidential data should be stored on local laptops unless approved and disk-encrypted.
- Retention and deletion:
  - Default telemetry: 90 days for raw logs, 2 years for aggregated metrics.
  - Customer data: retained per contract SLA; standard retention is 365 days unless otherwise specified.
  - Data deletion requests: follow privacy playbook and verify with Legal.
- Data minimization: Services should collect the minimum necessary fields; PII must be hashed/anonymized where possible.
- Backups: Backups containing Confidential/Sensitive data must be encrypted and tracked; retention follows backup policy (90/365/730 day tiers depending on service criticality).
- Data classification workflow: Teams must tag datasets in the catalog with classification and retention labels on creation.

4) Procurement and expenses
- Procurement thresholds and approval matrix:
  - <$2,000: Manager approval.
  - $2,000–$25,000: Department head + Finance approval.
  - >$25,000: Procurement + Finance + Legal review; purchase order required.
- Preferred vendors: Use approved vendor list in vendor management doc. Exceptions require a documented business case and Legal sign-off.
- Reimbursement policy for expenses:
  - Use company card when possible. Personal expenses require receipts and an expense report within 30 days.
  - Per diem: Domestic travel $75/day meal cap, International varies by country (see expense template).
  - Non-reimbursable: Alcohol (except client entertainment with pre-approval), personal items, unauthorized upgrades.
- Purchase order flow (example):
  1. Submit request in procurement portal with justification and cost center.
  2. Finance verifies budget and issues PO.
  3. Vendor receives PO; goods/services validated on receipt.
  4. Invoice routed to AP with PO reference.
- Capital vs. operating expenses: Finance will classify; major hardware purchases require CAPEX approval.

5) Vendor management (selection, onboarding, offboarding, SLAs)
- Vendor selection checklist:
  - Business justification, SOW, security questionnaire, pricing comparison, and reference checks.
  - For vendors handling customer data or production access: must pass InfoSec vendor assessment.
- Onboarding steps:
  1. Contract and NDA signed.
  2. Security assessment completed and approved.
  3. Access scoped and time-boxed; credentials issued via vault where possible.
  4. Vendor contact and escalation plan documented.
- SLAs and monitoring: Define service-level expectations (uptime, API latency, support response times) in SOW. Periodic vendor reviews (quarterly for critical vendors) and KPIs tracking.
- Offboarding: Revoke all credentials, rotate shared secrets, confirm data deletion/return per contract, and record final invoice reconciliation.

6) Travel policy (corporate travel and events)
- Booking rules: Use company travel portal for flights and hotels. Lowest reasonable fare and standard hotel policy unless a business justification is provided.
- Approvals: Manager approval required for travel >$500 or overnight stays. International travel requires People Ops and Security notification for visa/health guidance.
- Safety and security: Check travel advisories; for high-risk locations obtain Security pre-approval and emergency contact plan.
- Expense reporting: Submit receipts within 30 days; uses corporate expense system with mobile receipt upload.
- Corporate card use: Cardholders must follow policy; lost/stolen cards reported to Finance immediately.

7) Internal templates and standard artifacts
- Purpose: Reduce friction and ensure consistent documentation and approvals. Templates available in the internal templates library (link: confluence:templates). Examples included below as ready-to-copy sections.
- Templates included in this doc:
  - Access Request Template (fields: requestor, resource, justification, duration, approver)
  - Change Request Template (fields: change summary, impact, rollback plan, tests, approvers)
  - Vendor Onboarding Checklist (fields: legal, security, finance items)
  - Expense Report Template (fields: date, category, amount, receipt link, project code)

8) Compliance, exceptions, and enforcement
- Exceptions: Temporary waivers may be granted by People Ops + Security with documented justification and expiration date.
- Non-compliance: May lead to revocation of privileges, disciplinary action, or legal escalation depending on severity.
- Enforcement: Regular audits (quarterly for access, annual for vendor/security/compliance). Findings tracked in remediation tickets with clear owners and SLA for remediation (30/90/180 day depending on severity).

9) Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
- Q: How long does an access request take?
  A: Simple requests typically <48 hours; requests requiring Security review can take up to 7 business days.
- Q: Who do I contact for emergency access?
  A: Oncall + Security (see oncall contacts page). Emergency access must be followed by a post-approval review.
- Q: How do I request a preferred vendor be added?
  A: Submit vendor intake form to Procurement with a business justification and reference vendors.

Revision history

Notes
- This document is intended to be a living policy. Teams should file change proposals via the change management process for updates to service-specific requirements.
